small_guidance:
- The conv (B=1024, OC=16, D=13, H=29, W=29) dominates; the fused post-conv kernel is already cheap. Add autotune configs that cover the actual S=10933 better — try BLOCK_S=8192/16384 with num_warps=8/16, num_stages=2, so the per-(B,group) program finishes in 1-2 chunks instead of 3-6.
- Switch the load layout so the contiguous axis (S) is the inner dim and use `eviction_policy='evict_first'` (already done) plus `tl.multiple_of`/`max_contiguous` hints on `s_cur` to improve vectorized loads.
large_guidance:
- Replace the torch Conv3d with a custom Triton conv kernel: im2col-style GEMM with one program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile), keeping OC=16 fully in registers (OC tile = 16) and tiling the 10933 output-spatial elements (BLOCK_M=64/128). Fold the conv bias, HardSwish, and the per-channel partial sums (sum and sum-of-squares for GroupNorm) into the same kernel epilogue so the activation tensor never needs a second pass.
- Use a two-kernel design: (1) fused conv+hardswish that also accumulates per-(B, C) sum and sumsq via atomics or a small reduction buffer; (2) tiny finalization kernel that computes group mean/var, applies γ/β, and writes (B, C). This eliminates the full re-read of the BxCxDxHxW activation that the current kernel performs.
- Use channels_last3d (NDHWC) layout for the conv output tiles so the C=16 axis is contiguous and the GEMM-K (IC·kD·kH·kW = 3·64 = 192) loads coalesce naturally.
